# Draft Customer Response

## Description

Draft a professional, empathetic response to a customer support case.

## Instructions

When asked to draft a customer response:

1. Acknowledge the customer's issue with empathy
2. Summarize your understanding of the problem (confirm details)
3. Provide a clear next step or resolution
4. Set expectations for timeline if the issue requires further investigation
5. Use a professional but warm tone

## Guidelines

- Never blame the customer
- Avoid jargon — use plain language
- If you need more information, ask specific questions (not open-ended)
- Always include a concrete next step
- Sign off with the agent's name
- Do not expose internal notes, security details, personal data, model output, or facts not present in the case
- Use a placeholder rather than inventing an agent name

## Tone Examples

- Good: "I'm sorry to hear your order arrived damaged. I can see order #12345 was delivered on June 5th."
- Bad: "Per our policy, damaged items must be reported within 48 hours."
